\section{Conclusion}

The question was whether weak one-plaquette heat-kernel tails can be promoted
to rare-defect estimates uniform over every microscopic boundary.  They
cannot.  A private-opposite-link construction realizes one central staple
against $m-1$ coherent staples.  The conditional law then concentrates on a
metric barycenter: one $m$th of the central distance is assigned to the
selected link and the remaining $(m-1)/m$ to the frustrated plaquette.  Below
that target distance the good-event probability has the exact exponent
$-m(b_*-\rho)^2$, and the conclusion persists throughout an open
positive-measure set of boundaries.

The same geometry makes each private opposite link have asymptotically
maximal total-variation influence on the selected link.  The microscopic
Dobrushin row condition therefore fails at sufficiently small heat time.
What fails is the worst-conditioning representation of dependence, not the
possibility of weak-coupling control.  A viable construction must keep the
frustrating boundary visible---by restricting it, averaging it with its
cost, integrating it into a block, or attaching it to a charged contour.
Establishing any such replacement, and transporting it through continuum and
spectral limits, remains a separate problem.
